ai_show_review.summary: Epic Dancin' jam, debut Friend Of The Devil, tight Pigpen percussion
ai_show_review.blurb: The March 21‑1970 Capitol Theater show erupts with an 18‑minute Dancin' In The Street jam and the first live performance of Friend Of The Devil. Jerry’s tone is immaculate, Phil’s bass melodic, and Pigpen adds spirited percussion on Katie Mae. Highlights also include Casey Jones, Cosmic Charlie and a soaring Not Fade Away into Turn On Your Lovelight.
ai_show_review.review: On March 21, 1970 at the Capitol Theater in Port Chester, the Dead delivered a late‑show that feels like a snapshot of their early‑70s renaissance. The set opens with a fiery Casey Jones before slipping into a marathon Dancin' In The Street that stretches past eighteen minutes, showcasing Garcia’s flawless lead tone and Lesh’s inventive, melodic bass. A standout moment arrives when the band unveils Friend Of The Devil for the first time live, followed by an intimate acoustic turn‑around featuring Easy Wind (highlighted by Bob Weir’s soaring solo) and a playful Katie Mae powered by Pigpen’s lively percussion. The second half rolls on with high‑octane energy – Cosmic Charlie rockets forward, Saint Stephen segues into a rousing Not Fade Away that bursts into Turn On Your Lovelight, and the night closes on Midnight Hour despite a slightly meandering finish. Across three audience recordings, listeners consistently note the show’s tight musicianship, exuberant crowd interaction, and the rare blend of folk‑rock storytelling with extended jams, making this performance a must‑hear snapshot of the band’s evolution.

best_recording.reason: Clear, well‑captured audience tape that includes the key moments (Dancin' jam, Friend Of The Devil debut, Katie Mae) with solid crowd ambience; despite a few missing early songs it offers the most complete listening experience.

key_highlights: 18‑minute Dancin' In The Street jam that locks the band into a high‑energy groove
First live performance of Friend Of The Devil, delivered with crisp vocals and tight interplay
Pigpen’s lively percussion on Katie Mae adds extra swing to the set
Not Fade Away → Turn On Your Lovelight transition provides a soaring close

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers perfect tone and flawless lead throughout, especially on the extended Dancin' jam and his crisp work on Casey Jones.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides melodic, inventive bass lines that drive the 18‑minute Dancin' improvisation.
band_performance.Bob: Weir shines with a soaring solo on Easy Wind and strong vocal harmonies on several numbers.
band_performance.Pigpen: Pigpen’s lively percussion adds extra swing to Katie Mae, energizing the crowd.
